text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1-hotshot experienced autoscaler lag -> queue depth spike. p95 request latency crossing 600ms, p99 spiking above 2.5s. SLO target: p99 < 1s. Full telemetry: https://dash.reddemo/redwood/alerts/1779992222
Alex W.: I'm looking at the pool now. Confirming customer-facing streaming RPCs are impacted (stalling on tail packets).
Samir: seeing large number of warmup failures in the logs during scale-up. Autoscaler requested 8 nodes, only 2 came up in the last 3m. Kube events show `FailedCreate` on hotshot nodes.
Jia Chen: attaching snippet from the node-controller logs:
```
E 2026-03-15T14:10:11Z node-controller: create instance failed: quota exceeded, err=InsufficientCapacity: Not enough capacity for flavor g5x.large
W 2026-03-15T14:10:38Z autoscaler: scale request queued, attempt=3
```
Maria G.: Customer impact: three customers reported degraded streaming responses, two of them are high-priority PLG trial accounts. Estimated % of traffic hitting degraded pool ~ 12%.
Platform Oncall: I'm taking oncall for mitigation. Quick questions: can we failover traffic to eu-west-1-dedicated-fallback pool automatically? What's the compatibility on model variants?
Alex W.: Fallback routing exists but is behind handshake gating. Compatible model version available (v2-quant) but performance delta visible. If we failover, we should enable degraded-mode streaming (no KV prefetch) to avoid tail stalls.
Samir: temp mitigation idea: 1) pause new hotshot allocations into that pool, 2) split incoming requests across fallback pool via routing policy, 3) trigger manual node launch in another AZ.
Jia Chen: Also seeing KV cache cold-path amplification. When instances fail to warmup their KV cache, per-request latency jumps on p99. We should reduce prefix caching TTLs for the duration to reduce cache misses.
ops-bot: Metric snapshot at 14:12: p50=110ms, p95=680ms (+230ms), p99=2.74s (+1.7s), queue_depth=128 -> steady growth from 17. Autoscaling events: 4 scale attempts in last 4m.
Platform Oncall: Can infra manually spawn a node with a different instance type to satisfy capacity? We need quick capacity fudge.
Alex W.: I can kick off a manual launch to az-b with g5x.medium (lower perf but will accept warmup). Command:
```
# infra CLI
infra instances create --pool eu-west-1-hotshot --type g5x.medium --count 4 --tags hotshot-urgent
```
Samir: I'll start the reroute. Routing rule change to split 30% to eu-west-1-fallback and 70% stay on primary to keep warmup going. Applying now.
Samir: `route update --pool eu-west-1-hotshot --split 70,30 --target eu-west-1-fallback` -> applied.
Maria G.: Notifying affected customers. Draft sent to CSM. No incident comms publicly yet.
Jia Chen: Running quick health check after reroute. p95 dropped to ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s, queue depth trending down to 46. Streaming stalls reduced but still seeing occasional tail spikes tied to cold KV hits.
ops-bot: Autoscaler status: pending quota checks; manual instances creation in progress; expected ready in ~3-5m.
Alex W.: Important: disable aggressive batching on this pool for the next 10m so slow workers don't create head-of-line blocking. Change config:
```
batcher.max_batch_size=4
batcher.timeout_ms=15
```
Samir: done. Also increased `streaming.max_concurrent` for fallback pool to accept more handoffs.
Platform Oncall: Good progress. Need to capture RCA breadcrumbs: why did autoscaler get capacity errors? Logging the `InsufficientCapacity` as highest priority. Assigning to infra team for follow-up.
Maria G.: CSM update: two customers reported 30-40% of requests delayed >2s. No data loss. We offered temporary credits.
Jia Chen: Observed that warmup handshake retries were at 12x for some containers due to a stale image tag; new nodes were stuck trying to pull an older quantized kernel image. Patching image tag should prevent future warmup timeouts.
Alex W.: Patch plan: 1) set autoscaler fallback image to `release-2026-03-10` which fixes kernel mismatch; 2) add a transient feature flag to bypass handshake gating for emergency routing; 3) add alert to detect `imagePullBackOff` floods earlier.
ops-bot: Manual instances are `running` now. Node warmup progress: 65% warmed, KV prefetch in progress. Queue depth down to 12.
Samir: p99 back under 1s for non-degraded traffic; global p99 still 1.05s because fallback has slightly higher tail. Will keep routing at 70/30 for 10 more minutes.
Platform Oncall: Prepare handoff in 15m to next oncall. Current mitigations: manual node add, routing split, reduced batching, image tag rollback. Followups: infra to root cause capacity/quota, runtime to fix image tag automation, platform to add faster routing bypass for emergency.
Maria G.: Filed incident ticket INC-2026-0315-07 with incident timeline and customer impact.
Jia Chen: Quick log snippet showing image mismatch:
```
E image-puller: manifest for tag release-2026-02-28 not found
W warmup: retries=9, kv_prefetch failed
```
Alex W.: tagging action items:
- infra: investigate quota/spot capacity (owner: Samir)
- runtime: image tag automation + warmup retries cap (owner: Jia Chen)
- platform: emergency routing bypass + routing playbook update (owner: Alex W.)
- docs/CSM: customer comms followup (owner: Maria G.)
Platform Oncall: OK I'm going to hand this to next oncall in 20m. Will post final metrics snapshot and set a follow-up meeting. Original pager: @oncall. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: FINAL SNAPSHOT at 14:40: p95=210ms, p99=890ms, queue_depth=3, manual_nodes_added=4, routing_split=70/30. Incident severity: Sev2 -> downgrade candidate.
Alex W.: Thanks all. Leaving notes in the incident doc. Handoff to next oncall scheduled at 15:00Z.
Samir: closing my live actions. I'll keep infra ticket open until quota root cause identified.
Jia Chen: I'll follow up on warmup metrics and add a regression alert for cold KV amplification.
Maria G.: I'll send a customer reconciliation email and update the CSMs.
Platform Oncall: Handoff complete. Next oncall ack: @Platform Oncall (next). :white_check_mark:
